rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 - two-year replicated field experiment (three 0.4 ha blocks) at Russell Ranch comparing SDI, DDI and furrow in organic processing tomato, with irrigation measured by flow meter and yield by machine harvest. Q2: Section 3.1 and Fig. 1b - SSD gave significant gains in IWP over furrow in both years with no significant yield decrease despite 17% (2015) and 36% (2016) less irrigation water applied. Q8: Discussion (Section 4, last paragraphs) - the authors state that the reduced wetting volume of SSD raises only short-term IWP measured as crop per unit of applied water, and that overall system water use efficiency must account for shifts in microbial activity, soil structure and SOC; Conclusions note the study covers only the two years after SSD installation. Q9: Fig. 1 caption - error bars indicate standard error for IWP means.
rows.notes: IWP computed from one method (yield divided by metered water applied); no triangulation. Soil moisture distribution (GWC) was measured but not analysed as the pathway for IWP (no evaporation or drainage measurement), so Q4 is no. Single site, single crop, plot scale. No stated requirement conditions for the IWP gain.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1 and 2.5 - replicated field trial with weed counts in ten randomized quadrats per treatment per block on one date each year. Q2: Section 3.3 and Fig. 3 - SSD treatments were highly effective at suppressing weeds with fewer than 0.15 weeds per square metre in both years; weed density was 30 times (2015) and 100 times (2016) higher in furrow than in drip treatments.
rows.notes: Weed density measured by quadrat counts only (one method). The Fig. 3 caption attributes suppression to reduced surface wetting preventing germination, but this is asserted rather than measured; GWC at 0-20 cm did not differ significantly between treatments (Table 2), so Q4 is no. Counts taken on a single date per year, but this is not stated as a limitation. Fig. 3 caption mentions only letter groupings, not error bars or dispersion, so Q9 is no. Single site, one crop, plot scale.

notes: Full text appears complete (supplementary figures not included). Study is a primary two-year field experiment on organic processing tomato comparing single and double subsurface drip configurations with furrow irrigation; both claims are directly supported by the study's own results.
